name.text: Determining the Surface Area of an Ice-Cream Cone Container

questiontext.text:
Mogaka, a Grade 10 student, sketches an ice-cream container made of a cone with a scoop of ice cream, a hemisphere, forming a dome on top, as shown in the diagram below.

[[jsxgraph]] const brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-9, 11, 9, -13], axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); const r = 6; // schematic radius (drawing only) const h = 10; // schematic cone height (drawing only) const k = 0.32; // vertical squash for the perspective ellipse // --- Hemisphere dome: upper semicircle sitting on the rim --- brd.create('curve', [ t => r * Math.cos(t), t => r * Math.sin(t), 0, Math.PI ], {strokeColor: '#1f3c88', strokeWidth: 2, fillColor: '#90caf9', fillOpacity: 0.7}); // --- Cone with the apex at the bottom --- const V = brd.create('point', [0, -h], {visible: false}); const Lp = brd.create('point', [-r, 0], {visible: false}); const Rp = brd.create('point', [ r, 0], {visible: false}); brd.create('segment', [V, Lp], {strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 2}); brd.create('segment', [V, Rp], {strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 2}); // --- Rim: the circle where the cone meets the hemisphere (drawn as a filled ellipse) --- brd.create('curve', [ t => r * Math.cos(t), t => k * r * Math.sin(t), 0, 2 * Math.PI ], {strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 1.5, fillColor: '#90caf9', fillOpacity: 0.7}); // --- Vertical height of the cone (dashed) --- const O = brd.create('point', [0, 0], {visible: false}); brd.create('segment', [V, O], {strokeColor: 'black', dash: 2}); // --- Base radius (dashed) --- brd.create('segment', [O, Rp], {strokeColor: 'black', dash: 2}); // --- Labels (show the randomised dimensions) --- brd.create('text', [0.4, -5, '{#height_of_the_cone#} cm'], {anchorX: 'left', fontSize: 14}); brd.create('text', [2.6, -1.2, '{#base_radius_of_the_cone#} cm'], {anchorX: 'left', fontSize: 14}); brd.create('text', [3.6, -4.7, '{#slantheight_of_the_cone#} cm'], {anchorX: 'left', fontSize: 14}); [[/jsxgraph]]

Take \(\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\). Determine the total (external) surface area of the ice-cream container, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.

\(\text{Total surface area}=\) [[input:ans1]] \(\,\text{cm}^2\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The container is made of two solids joined at a circle: a cone and a hemisphere. Only the curved surfaces are exposed; the circular face where the cone and hemisphere meet is inside the solid, so it is not part of the surface area.

From the diagram, with \(\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\):
Radius \(r = {@base_radius_of_the_cone@}\) cm
Vertical height \(h = {@height_of_the_cone@}\) cm
Slant height \(l = {@slantheight_of_the_cone@}\) cm

Step 1: Curved surface area of the cone

\( \begin{align} \text{Curved surface area of cone} &= \pi r l \\ &= \frac{22}{7} \times {@base_radius_of_the_cone@} \times {@slantheight_of_the_cone@} \\ &= \frac{22}{7} \times {@R_times_l@} \\ &= {@Area_cone@}\ \text{cm}^2 \end{align} \)

Step 2: Curved surface area of the hemisphere

\( \begin{align} \text{Curved surface area of hemisphere} &= 2 \pi r^2 \\ &= 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times ({@base_radius_of_the_cone@})^2 \\ &= 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times {@R1@} \\ &= {@Hemisphere_area@}\ \text{cm}^2 \end{align} \)

Step 3: Total surface area

Keep full accuracy until the last line, then round to 2 decimal places:
\( \begin{align} \text{Total surface area} &= \pi r l + 2\pi r^2 \\ &= {@Area_cone@} + {@Hemisphere_area@} \\ &= {@Surface_Area@}\ \text{cm}^2 \end{align} \)

questionnote.text: \(r={@base_radius_of_the_cone@}\) cm, \(h={@height_of_the_cone@}\) cm, \(l={@slantheight_of_the_cone@}\) cm; total surface area \(={@Surface_Area@}\ \text{cm}^2\).

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

node.description: Used the surface area of a whole sphere instead of a hemisphere.

truefeedback.text: You have used the curved surface area of a whole sphere, \(4\pi r^2\). Only the exposed hemisphere should be included, and the circular face where it meets the cone is internal, so it is not counted.

node.description: Included the circular base of the cone.

truefeedback.text: You have included the circular base of the cone, \(\pi r^2\). Because the cone is joined to the hemisphere at that circle, the face is internal and is not part of the external surface area. Use only the curved surface of the cone, plus the curved part of the hemisphere.

node.description: Found the volume of the solid instead of the surface area.

truefeedback.text: It looks like you have found the volume of the container, \(\tfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h + \tfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3\), rather than its surface area. Volume measures the space inside (in \(\text{cm}^3\)); here you need the area of the outside surface (in \(\text{cm}^2\)).

falsefeedback.text:
Not quite. The external surface is the curved surface of the cone plus the curved surface of the hemisphere:

Use \(\pi=\tfrac{22}{7}\) and give your answer to 2 decimal places.

qtest.description: Correct answer (to 2 d.p.) gets full marks.
Whole-sphere mistake is diagnosed and scores 0.
Including the cone's base is diagnosed and scores 0.
An unrecognised wrong answer falls through to the general hint.
Finding the volume instead of the surface area is diagnosed and scores 0.
